clips.send: Yueyang Tower. Today: Yueyang, Hunan. A three-storey wooden tower on the city wall above Dongting Lake. Fan Zhongyan wrote “先天下之忧而忧, 后天下之乐而乐” for it — without ever climbing it himself.

clips.send: Humble Room. Today: He County, Anhui. Tradition says Liu Yuxi wrote 《陋室铭》 while governor of Hezhou, where the town gave him only a tiny room. A rebuilt “humble room” stands in He County today.

clips.send: Old Drunkard’s Pavilion. Today: Mount Langya, Chuzhou, Anhui. The monk Zhixian built it and Ouyang Xiu named it after himself. With its wing-like roof corners (翼然) it is one of China’s four famous pavilions.

clips.send: Zhuge Liang’s Hut, Nanyang. Today: Wolonggang, Nanyang, Henan. Zhuge Liang lived in a thatched hut until Liu Bei came three times to ask for his help. Both Nanyang (Henan) and Longzhong near Xiangyang (Hubei) claim the hut.

clips.send: Mount Lu. Today: Jiujiang, Jiangxi. A misty mountain by the Yangtze and Poyang Lake. Li Bai’s waterfall “飞流直下三千尺” and Su Shi’s “不识庐山真面目” were both written about it.

clips.send: Hundred-Plant Garden and Three-Flavour Study. Today: Lu Xun’s Native Place, Shaoxing, Zhejiang. The garden behind Lu Xun’s family home and, across a little river, the old private school where he studied. Both can still be visited — compare them with his essay!

clips.send: Yellow Crane Tower. Today: Snake Hill, Wuchang, Wuhan. A tower on Snake Hill above the Yangtze, first built about 1,800 years ago. Legend says an immortal flew away from it on a yellow crane.

clips.send: 易错点：一句话可以同时用几种修辞：“苔痕上阶绿，草色入帘青”既是对偶，又是拟人（“上”“入”）；“孔子云：何陋之有？”既是引用，又是反问。答题时要看题目问的是哪一种。
